messages:
customer-alerts: Hi Redwood — heads up, we see unexpected KMS Decrypts against our private key (arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01). Seems to be from an unknown principal around 2026-03-18T03:45:00Z. We think there may have been access to decrypted payloads. Can you pull audit logs and confirm? Ticket #SEC-6721

ingrid: Sorry to hear that. Can you confirm the earliest observed timestamp and any correlation IDs? We'll escalate to SecOps and start a log pull. Do you want us to share logs here or a secure bundle? :shield:

customer-alerts: Earliest timestamp 2026-03-18T03:43:12Z. Correlation IDs: trace=6f9a...; requestId=9d2c. Please put logs in the secure bundle.

security-bot: [automated] Alert created: SEC-6721. Priority: HIGH. Notifying secops and infra oncall.

katelyn: Assigned. Can you confirm this is on Redwood Private (VPC) or Dedicated for you? Also, do you have any recent RBAC changes we should be aware of?

customer-alerts: It's our Private deployment (VPC). No RBAC changes on our side in the last 7 days. We rotated service account creds last month.

raj: I'll start pulling control-plane and node-level audit logs from the customer's private control plane. Plan: 1) KMS CloudTrail events 2) control-plane audit logs 3) VPC flow logs 4) egress/NAT gateway logs 5) S3 access logs for that timeframe. Will collect as a sanitized bundle. ETA 60m.

maria: Quick note — sometimes our internal rotation job (redwood-private-rotator) will call KMS:Decrypt during key rewraps. I'll grep the rotator logs for that timeframe and post findings.

maria: Found two decrypt events at 2026-03-18T03:43:11Z and 2026-03-18T03:45:08Z. Principal: arn:aws:iam::444455556666:role/redwood-private-rotator. RequestIDs: 9d2c..., a3f1... Snippet from control-plane audit: 
```
{"eventTime":"2026-03-18T03:43:11Z","eventName":"Decrypt","userIdentity":{"arn":"arn:aws:iam::444455556666:role/redwood-private-rotator","type":"Role"},"requestParameters":{"keyId":"abcd-ef01"},"responseElements":{"decryptionContext":"key-rotation"}}
```

katelyn: That's helpful. Maria — can you confirm whether the rotator process runs with access scoped to that tenant's key or a shared service principal? If it's a shared principal we need to check key policy scoping.

maria: Rotator runs as a shared service role but KMS key policy is supposed to require key-specific grants. For this key, I see an explicit Grant for the shared role — looks like prior onboarding allowed it.

ingrid: Customer asked if any data left the VPC. Raj — any signs of egress to external IPs matched to those requestIDs?

raj: I've checked VPC flow logs and NAT gateway logs for the two timestamps. No large outbound transfers near those times. There are short control-plane connections to our internal telemetry endpoints (port 443) which are expected. S3 access logs show no GetObject for tenant bucket during window.

katelyn: TL;DR so far: KMS decrypts were performed by our rotator role due to an onboarding grant. No evidence of exfil (no S3 reads, no unusual NAT egress). Next actions: 1) rotate the affected KMS key ASAP (customer consent?) 2) replace Grant so rotator uses a tenant-scoped invocation pattern 3) produce sanitized audit bundle for customer and for SOC 4) add detection rule for cross-tenant decrypts.

customer-alerts: Please rotate the key and regenerate any dependent ciphertext. We want key rotation and a post-incident report. Also please remove the Grant if it isn't tenant-scoped.

katelyn: Understood. Raj will perform a scheduled key rotation and we'll re-run onboarding to scope access. Raj — coordinate a maintenance window with the customer; we should provide rollback instructions.

raj: Scheduling rotation for 2026-03-18T05:00:00Z in maintenance mode. I'll also create an IAM policy template to limit rotator to tenant-specific keys. We'll send the sanitized logs bundle to the secure file share (link will be S3 presigned — customer alerted).

maria: Post-rotation verification: I rechecked decrypt counts after rotation and see 0 unexpected decrypts. Also raised a PR to change onboarding to avoid granting broad rights to shared role (ref: github.com/redwood/rotator/pull/482).

katelyn: I'll write the incident summary for SOC and the customer mmr (minimal measurable report). Key points: root cause = pre-existing onboarding grant that allowed shared rotator role to decrypt tenant key; impact = no confirmed data exfil; corrective = rotate key, tighten onboarding RBAC, add detection; follow-ups = post-mortem and update runbook.

customer-alerts: Thanks — appreciate the quick response. Please include timestamps and the requestIDs in the final report.

katelyn: Will do. Deliverables: sanitized audit bundle (raj), PR to onboarding (maria), rotated key + rotation notes (raj), incident report (katelyn). Closing thread after report is posted. :white_check_mark:
